problem_description: Compute the average temperature in K and pressure in bar for a system containing the 101 hydrogen molecule. The hydrogen molecule should be modeled using the gromos54a7_atb.ff force field. Periodic boundary conditions should be applied in all directions. First, energy minimization was performed using the steepest descent algorithm. The energy minimization was carried out for a maximum of 50,000 steps. Electrostatic interactions were treated using a cut-off scheme with a Coulomb cutoff (rcoulomb) of 1.0 nm, while van der Waals interactions were calculated using a cut-off scheme with a cutoff (rvdw) of 1.0 nm. The Verlet cutoff scheme was used, and periodic boundary conditions were applied in all directions. This was followed by an equilibration phase in the NVT ensemble using the MD integrator. A time step of 0.00025 ps was used, and the NVT equilibration was performed for 10,000,000 steps, corresponding to a total simulation time of 2500 ps. During the NVT equilibration, all bonds were constrained. The Verlet cutoff scheme was used, with electrostatic interactions treated using a Coulomb cut-off scheme with a Coulomb cutoff (rcoulomb) of 1.0 nm, while van der Waals interactions were calculated using a cut-off scheme with a cutoff (rvdw) of 1.0 nm. Temperature coupling was performed using the V-rescale thermostat with the entire system treated as a single temperature-coupling group (tc-grps = System) to maintain the temperature at 300 K with a temperature coupling constant (τₜ) of 0.1 ps. The average temperature and pressure should be calculated from the production run.
